- If sentiment is positive (≥0.2) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slope or cap upward momentum.
- If sentiment is negative (≤0.0), model often underestimates; adjust downward bias, especially if recent prices are falling.
- Model consistently overpredicts after sharp upward spikes (e.g., 89.37 → 89.70+), suggesting overshoot; apply downward correction after peak.
- If true outcome shows strong mean reversion (e.g., 89.37 → 82.26 → 85.32), model fails to capture volatility decay; reduce forecast slope after 3–5 days of high prices.
- For 30-day forecasts, model often fails to account for sentiment-driven volatility; if sentiment is volatile, add 1–2% downward buffer to forecast.
- If sentiment history shows repeated 0.00 values, model tends to be flat or slightly upward; if true outcome drops, adjust downward by 1–3% for next 5–7 days.
- Model overestimates in early forecast window (first 5–7 days) when sentiment is neutral or positive; reduce initial forecast by 0.5–1.5% to align with true volatility.
